requirement:
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.authoring.invocation`, so no implementation root is needed. The review roots list is empty. Every clause specifies behavior that can be observed from outside.

- The command form `habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]` is a CLI syntax. A different argument parser, or a different internal command type, would accept and reject the same invocations. Parser choice is discretionary.
- "MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current project under `requirements.authoring.refresh`" governs which subject is chosen. `requirements.authoring.refresh` and `requirements.authoring.reassessment` are cited for context. They are judged on their own text and are not delegated here. No library, type or interface is named.
- "MUST report the selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on completion" is about output content. Any code that prints those values meets it.
- "The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected" is about output content. Any code that prints the right destination meets it.
- "In stdout mode, the completion report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr" is about which output stream is used. Any code that writes there meets it.
- "`author-evidence` MUST remain an alias for the single-subject command" is observable. An implementation could register `author-evidence` as a separate subcommand that behaves the same way, or as a clap alias. Both give identical results. The requirement does not say how the alias is wired.

Each clause could be met by a different internal design that behaves the same, so none is a structural obligation.

behavioral: The marked tests cover each behavioral obligation in `requirements.authoring.invocation`.

- **Selecting one existing subject.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template]` runs `author` on both a requirement and a named example. For each it checks the subject line, the evidence record, and which field is present.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[author_rejects_unknown_subjects_and_conflicting_targets]` shows an absent name fails and names the subject. It also shows that giving both a subject and `--all` conflicts, and that existing evidence is left unchanged.
- **Selecting under the refresh rules.** `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` covers the `--missing` default, `--force` and `--stdout`, and it covers `--missing` and `--force` being mutually exclusive. It also covers the `author-evidence` alias and the "skipped as current" report. Those details belong to `requirements.authoring.refresh`. This test is marked for it and for the subject.
- **Reporting on completion.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` asserts that stdout starts with `SUBJECT: ollama / MODEL`. It also asserts an `Evidence:` line whose path resolves to `evidence/<subject>.json`, and a `Usage:` line.
  - `initial_prompt_substitutes_subject_and_mandatory_inputs_into_the_template` repeats these checks for requirement and example subjects. It also checks that the usage path is an existing file.
- **Stdout mode.**
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files]` parses stdout as pure evidence JSON and checks that project files are unchanged. It asserts stderr carries the subject/backend/model line, `Evidence: stdout`, and the `Usage:` path. It also checks that the false and FIXME judgments appear on stderr only.
  - `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence]` checks that stdout stays empty on failure in `--stdout` mode, so diagnostics go to stderr.
- **Options and alias.**
  - `--config` is exercised by `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]`, which asserts the alternate profile's model and key are used.
  - `-v` and `--verbose` are exercised by `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs]` and the verbose cases of the stdout test.
  - `author-evidence` is used as the command in the main CLI, stdout, and submission tests. It is also rejected with `--all`, which fits its being the single-subject alias.
- **Subsequent assessments.** The text only says these follow `requirements.authoring.reassessment`. That requirement is cited as context, so I did not reassess its tests here.

I found no unexercised obligation, and the assertions enforce the expected outcomes.

text: :::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST initially select one existing requirement or named example in the current
project under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. Subsequent assessments
follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} refresh
Every `habeas author` form MUST accept `--missing` and `--force`, which are
mutually exclusive; `--missing` MUST be the default. Under `--missing`, the
command MUST initially assess only the selected subjects whose evidence is missing, stale,
or invalid, and MUST preserve every current record without invoking a model,
including accepted FIXME judgments and current false judgments; a current false
judgment is reassessed only when its subject or inputs change or `--force` is
given. Under `--force`, the command MUST assess every selected subject. `--stdout`
MUST imply `--force`, because it writes no evidence. The command MUST report the
number of selected subjects it skipped as current on initial selection.
After that selection, {cite}`requirements.authoring.reassessment` governs each round. When no assessment is needed,
the command MUST succeed without resolving model configuration or credentials.
:::{req} reassessment
After applying a round's additions, Habeas MUST check freshness against the
edited sources. It MUST reassess a subject whose corrections are all satisfied
when the writes changed its assessment inputs. It MUST also reassess any other
subject whose previously current evidence those writes made stale, including
definitions, citation reviews, and site reviews outside the initial selection.
Independent reassessments MUST run under {cite}`requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
Each reassessment MUST use fresh inputs and the selected assessment policy.
Only a fresh successful assessment establishes `true`.
A subject with a remaining manual instruction or an action that could not be applied MUST pause for
the rest of the invocation, even if another edit changes its inputs. Other
subjects MUST continue. An already-present marker or stale selector alone MUST
cause no reassessment. If every requested marker already exists and the inputs
are unchanged, the negative judgment stands. Repeat while eligible subjects
remain, with no limit on rounds or automated additions. With `--stdout`, Habeas
MUST report the named subject's assessment and proposed corrections without
editing sources or starting a correction-driven reassessment.
